definitions.explanation: A style of painting based on traditional Japanese artistic conventions, techniques, and materials such as mineral pigments, ink, and washi paper or silk. Distinguished from Western-style painting (洋画) as a category in the Japanese art world.

examples.japanese: ⟦{美術館|びじゅつかん}→美術館：01717_bijutsukan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{日本画|にほんが}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{展覧会|てんらんかい}→展覧会：01470_tenrankai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a Japanese painting exhibition at the art museum.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{日本画|にほんが}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{専攻|せんこう}→専攻：01587_senkou⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。

examples.japanese: {日本画|にほんが}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{岩絵具|いわえのぐ}や⟦{墨|すみ}→墨：02155_sumi⟧⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦{天然|てんねん}→天然：03560_tennen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{素材|そざい}→素材：09492_sozai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{描|えが}かれる→描く：02013_egaku⟧。
examples.english: Japanese-style paintings are created using natural materials such as mineral pigments and ink.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The term {日本画|にほんが} was coined in the Meiji period to distinguish traditional Japanese painting from newly introduced Western-style painting (⟦{洋画|ようが}→洋画：14741_youga⟧). This distinction remains important in the Japanese art world, where art departments, exhibitions, and competitions are often divided into {日本画|にほんが} and ⟦{洋画|ようが}→洋画：14741_youga⟧ categories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本画|にほんが}{家|か} (Japanese-style painter)
- {日本画|にほんが}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{技法|ぎほう}→技法：12800_gihou⟧ (Japanese painting techniques)
- {日本画|にほんが}⟦{展|てん}→〜展：28468_ten⟧ (Japanese painting exhibition)
- ⟦{現代|げんだい}→現代：02722_gendai⟧{日本画|にほんが} (contemporary Japanese-style painting)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{洋画|ようが}→洋画：14741_youga⟧: Western-style painting — the counterpart category using oil paints, canvas, and Western techniques
- ⟦{水墨画|すいぼくが}→水墨画：27810_suibokuga⟧: ink wash painting — a specific type within {日本画|にほんが} using only black ink
